stem: Plants in larger containers remain wet longer than plants in smaller containers using the same media and irrigation frequency. Why is this plausible?
choices: Container volume and geometry can change the amount and distribution of stored water relative to root occupancy
Larger containers always have lower EC
Root-zone water is independent of container geometry
rationale: Container size and root occupancy affect water storage and depletion patterns, so identical schedules can create different root-zone states.
